Check: Default zone policy set to No Access
GUI: Web Tools / SANnav: Zoning > Default Zone
Expected (Pass): CLI: defzone --show returns 'Default Zone: No Access' | GUI: Default Zone field shows 'No Access'
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: defzone --show returns 'Default Zone: All Access' | GUI: Default Zone field shows 'All Access' — any unzoned device can communicate with any other

Check: No multi-initiator zones (exactly 1 initiator WWN per zone)
GUI: Web Tools: Zoning > Zone Admin — review member counts
Expected (Pass): CLI: Each zone in zoneshow contains exactly 1 host HBA WWN and 1+ target WWNs | GUI: Zone member count shows 2 entries (1 initiator + 1 target) per single-target zone
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: zoneshow shows zone with 2+ host HBA WWNs as members | GUI: Zone shows multiple initiator WWNs — hosts can scan each other's LUNs

Check: No zones with wildcard or all membership
Expected (Pass): CLI: No * characters in any zone member list in zoneshow output | GUI: All zones show specific WWN or alias names only
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: zoneshow output contains * in member list or zone has unusually large member count | GUI: Zone member list contains wildcard entry

Check: No stale zones (WWNs not present in fabric)
Expected (Pass): CLI: All WWNs listed in zoneshow appear in nsshow nameserver output | GUI: SANnav Unused Zone Members report returns 0 entries
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: WWNs exist in zoneshow that are absent from nsshow — decommissioned HBAs still in zones | GUI: SANnav report lists orphaned WWNs with no matching fabric device

Check: Zone aliases used for all WWNs
GUI: Web Tools: Zoning > Zone Admin > Aliases
Expected (Pass): CLI: alishow shows alias for every WWN; zoneshow shows alias names not raw WWNs | GUI: Zone Admin displays human-readable names (e.g. ESX01_HBA0) not hex WWNs
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: zoneshow shows raw WWNs like 10:00:00:90:fa:1a:2b:3c with no alias | GUI: Zone Admin shows unreadable hex strings making audit difficult

Check: DH-CHAP enabled on all ISLs / E-ports
Expected (Pass): CLI: authutil --show returns 'Policy: on' and 'Auth Type: dh-chap' | GUI: Authentication policy shows 'Active' or 'Enforced'
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: authutil --show returns 'Policy: off' or 'Auth Type: none' | GUI: Authentication shows 'Off' or 'None' — rogue switches can join fabric unauthenticated

Check: SCC policy active (only known switches can join fabric)
Expected (Pass): CLI: sccpolicyshow returns a list of permitted switch WWNs | GUI: SCC Policy shows a populated list of authorised switches
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: sccpolicyshow returns 'SCC_POLICY: none' or empty | GUI: SCC Policy blank or shows 'No Policy' — any switch can join fabric

Check: DCC policy active (only known devices on specific ports)
Expected (Pass): CLI: dccpolicyshow returns device-to-port mappings for all fabric ports | GUI: DCC Policy shows populated port/device bindings
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: dccpolicyshow returns empty or 'DCC_POLICY: none' | GUI: DCC Policy blank — any device can connect to any port

Check: No unauthorized switches in fabric
Expected (Pass): CLI: fabricshow lists only known switch WWNs and domain IDs matching your asset register | GUI: Inventory > Switches shows only expected devices with known names
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: fabricshow shows unfamiliar switch WWN or unexpected domain ID | GUI: Unknown switch appears in inventory without a recognised hostname

Check: Telnet disabled
Expected (Pass): CLI: ipfilter --show shows no permit rule for port 23; telnet connection refused | GUI: Protocols page shows Telnet: Disabled
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: ipfilter --show shows permit for port 23; telnet <switch-ip> connects successfully | GUI: Telnet listed as Enabled — credentials transmitted in cleartext

Check: HTTP disabled (HTTPS only)
GUI: Web Tools: Switch Admin > Security > Protocols
Expected (Pass): CLI: httpscertshow shows valid cert; curl to port 80 returns connection refused or redirects to HTTPS | GUI: Protocols page shows HTTP: Disabled / HTTPS: Enabled
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: curl http://<switch-ip> returns HTTP 200 with no redirect | GUI: HTTP listed as Enabled — management traffic sent in cleartext

Check: Default admin password changed
CLI Command: Cannot verify via CLI — confirm with team
Expected (Pass): CLI: Attempting login with factory default password (e.g. 'password') fails | GUI: User record shows password last changed after initial deployment date
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: Login with default credentials succeeds | GUI: Password change date matches factory/installation date — never changed

Check: No shared or generic accounts
Expected (Pass): CLI: All accounts in userconfig --show -a are individually named (e.g. j.smith, b.jones) | GUI: User list shows only personal named accounts
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: Accounts named 'admin' / 'oper' / 'readonly' present and used by multiple people | GUI: Generic account names visible with no individual owner

Check: RBAC roles correctly assigned (least-privilege)
Expected (Pass): CLI: Operators show role: operator; only designated admins show role: admin or securityadmin | GUI: Roles column shows varied roles appropriate to each user's function
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: Most or all accounts show role: admin regardless of function | GUI: All users assigned Administrator role — no role separation

Check: SSH-only remote access (Telnet blocked)
Expected (Pass): CLI: sshutil --show shows SSH enabled; ipfilter shows port 22 open and port 23 absent/blocked | GUI: SSH: Enabled and Telnet: Disabled on protocols page
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: Port 23 open in ipfilter; telnet connection to switch succeeds | GUI: Telnet shown as Enabled alongside SSH

Check: Management IP access restricted by ACL to management subnet
GUI: Web Tools: Switch Admin > IP Filter
Expected (Pass): CLI: ipfilter --show shows permit rules limited to management subnet CIDR (e.g. 10.10.0.0/24); all other sources denied | GUI: IP Filter shows restrictive rules with management VLAN range only
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: ipfilter --show shows 'permit tcp any any' or no deny rules | GUI: IP Filter shows any/any rules or is empty — management reachable from any host

Check: Audit logging enabled
Expected (Pass): CLI: auditcfg --show returns filter entries covering AUTH / ZONE / SECURITY / FIRMWARE event classes | GUI: Audit Config shows Enabled with event categories ticked
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: auditcfg --show returns empty filter list or shows 'disabled' | GUI: Audit Config shows Disabled or no categories selected — security events not recorded

Check: Syslog configured to remote SIEM
Expected (Pass): CLI: syslogdipadd list returns one or more SIEM IP addresses | GUI: Syslog page shows remote server IP configured with appropriate facility/severity
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: syslogdipadd list returns empty — no remote destination | GUI: Syslog page shows no remote server configured — logs stored locally only and may be lost

Check: Firmware at current supported level (check Broadcom CVEs)
Expected (Pass): CLI: version returns FOS version matching or above Broadcom's current recommended release with no open CVEs | GUI: SANnav firmware column matches current Broadcom release
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: version returns outdated FOS version with published CVEs | GUI: SANnav flags firmware as outdated or below minimum supported level

Check: No volumes presented to wildcard / all-hosts
GUI: SSMC: Block Persona > Virtual Volumes > Exports — filter by host
Expected (Pass): CLI: showvlun -t shows every row has a specific named hostname in the Host column | GUI: Exports list shows all volumes assigned to named hosts — no blank or wildcard host entries
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: showvlun -t shows Host = * or blank host field for one or more LUNs | GUI: Export entry shows host field as '*' or 'All Hosts' — any connected host can access the volume

Check: Each ESX host or cluster in its own host set
GUI: SSMC: Block Persona > Hosts > Host Sets
Expected (Pass): CLI: showhostset shows host sets aligned 1:1 to clusters; no mixing of hosts from different environments | GUI: Host Sets view shows logically named sets containing only hosts from the same cluster
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: showhostset shows production and dev/test ESX hosts in the same host set | GUI: Host sets contain mixed or ungrouped hosts from different clusters or environments

Check: LUN 0 not presented to ESX hosts
GUI: SSMC: Virtual Volumes > Exports — sort by LUN ID
Expected (Pass): CLI: showvlun -t shows no entries where LUN column = 0 for VMware hosts | GUI: Exports sorted by LUN ID shows lowest LUN for VMware hosts is 1 or higher
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: showvlun -t shows lun=0 mapped to a VMware host | GUI: LUN 0 visible in VMware host export list — can cause rescan issues and unexpected device enumeration

Check: iSCSI ports use mutual CHAP (if iSCSI in use)
Expected (Pass): CLI: showiscsisession shows AuthMethod: CHAP (Mutual) for all sessions | GUI: iSCSI port config shows CHAP: Mutual with initiator and target secrets configured
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: showiscsisession shows AuthMethod: None | GUI: iSCSI port shows CHAP: Disabled or None — initiator can connect without authentication

Check: Default Administrator account disabled or renamed
Expected (Pass): CLI: showuser -d Administrator returns 'Account status: Disabled' or 'User not found' | GUI: Administrator account shows Disabled status or does not appear in user list
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: showuser -d Administrator returns 'Account status: Enabled' | GUI: Administrator account shows Active/Enabled — well-known default credential is a target for attackers

Check: Named accounts only (no shared credentials)
Expected (Pass): CLI: showuser lists only individually owned accounts (e.g. firstname.lastname or role-specific service accounts with documented owners) | GUI: Users list shows named individuals with clear ownership
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: showuser lists generic accounts like 'admin' / 'backup_user' / 'monitoring' used by multiple people | GUI: Generic account names with no individual owner visible in user list

Check: Least-privilege roles assigned (no unnecessary super role)
Expected (Pass): CLI: showuser -d <username> shows role: browse or edit for non-admins; super role limited to designated storage admins only | GUI: Roles column shows varied roles (Browse / Edit / Administrator) — not all Super
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: showuser -d backup_user shows role: super | GUI: All users show Super or Administrator role — no role separation between admin and operator functions

Check: MFA enabled (if SSMC version supports it)
CLI Command: showsys (check version); auth policy via SSMC only
Expected (Pass): CLI: showsys confirms SSMC version supports MFA | GUI: Authentication Policies shows MFA: Required or Enabled for all admin logins
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: Version supports MFA but policy not enforced | GUI: Authentication Policies shows MFA: Disabled or not configured — password-only login accepted

Check: API client credentials rotated and inventoried
Expected (Pass): CLI: N/A | GUI: API Clients list shows all clients with known owners; last-rotated dates within policy window (e.g. 90 days)
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: N/A | GUI: API clients show creation dates months or years old with no rotation record — stale credentials that may be broadly shared

Check: Audit logging enabled and shipped to SIEM
Expected (Pass): CLI: showsys -detail shows syslog server IP configured with event categories enabled | GUI: Event Log Settings shows remote syslog IP and event types selected
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: showsys -detail shows no remote syslog target | GUI: Event Log Settings shows no remote server — logs only stored locally and may roll over without SIEM visibility

Check: Management interface on OOB / management VLAN only
Expected (Pass): CLI: shownet shows management IP in a dedicated management subnet (e.g. 10.0.0.x) isolated from data and VM VLANs | GUI: Network config shows management IP on a separate VLAN with no overlap with storage or VM subnets
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: shownet shows management IP on same subnet as ESX data or VM traffic | GUI: Management IP shares VLAN or subnet with data network — management plane reachable from untrusted hosts

Check: HTTPS only for SSMC / REST API (TLS 1.2+)
Expected (Pass): CLI: showcert shows valid cert with future expiry; openssl shows TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3; port 80 refused | GUI: Certificate Management shows green valid cert; no HTTP access possible
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: openssl shows TLSv1.0/1.1 negotiated or cert is expired; port 80 responds with HTTP 200 | GUI: Certificate shows expired or near-expiry warning; HTTP accessible

Check: Firmware at current HPE supported level
Expected (Pass): CLI: showsys returns firmware version matching HPE's current SPP release with no open advisories | GUI: Software Versions page shows version matching HPE Support Center current recommended release
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: showsys returns firmware version behind HPE's current release | GUI: Software Versions shows outdated version; HPE advisory warnings may appear

Check: Snapshot schedules have retention limits set
Expected (Pass): CLI: showsched shows each schedule with a defined expiry/retain value (e.g. retain: 30d) | GUI: Schedules list shows a retention period populated for every schedule
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: showsched shows retain: unlimited or no expiry field for one or more schedules | GUI: Schedule entry shows 'No expiration' or blank retention — snapshots accumulate indefinitely and can exhaust pool capacity

Check: Replication traffic encrypted (if remote copy in use)
Expected (Pass): CLI: showrcopy shows Encryption: enabled for each replication link | GUI: Remote Copy links show Encryption: Enabled in link details
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: showrcopy shows Encryption: none or disabled | GUI: Remote Copy links show Encryption: None — replication data transmitted in cleartext between sites

Check: Replication peer authentication configured (not none)
GUI: SSMC: Data Protection > Remote Copy > Targets
Expected (Pass): CLI: showrcopy targets shows auth method (e.g. chap) for each peer — not 'none' | GUI: Remote Copy Targets show Authentication: Configured with a defined method
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: showrcopy targets shows auth: none for one or more peers | GUI: Target authentication field shows 'None' — peer can replicate without authentication

Check: ESX hosts only enumerate their assigned LUNs (no cross-visibility)
CLI Command: esxcli storage san fc list; esxcli storage core path list
GUI: vCenter: Host > Configure > Storage Adapters > Targets
Expected (Pass): CLI: esxcli storage core path list shows only paths to LUNs in the host's assigned host group; target count matches expected | GUI: Storage Adapters > Targets shows only the assigned Alletra array and correct LUN count
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: esxcli storage core path list shows paths to LUNs belonging to other host groups or unexpected arrays | GUI: Unexpected targets or additional LUNs visible beyond what is assigned to this host

Check: NPIV disabled if not actively used
CLI Command: esxcli storage san fc npiv list
GUI: vCenter: Host > Configure > Storage Adapters — check for NPIV ports
Expected (Pass): CLI: esxcli storage san fc npiv list returns empty / no output | GUI: Storage Adapters shows no NPIV virtual ports listed under physical HBAs
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: esxcli storage san fc npiv list returns one or more NPIV virtual port entries | GUI: NPIV ports visible under storage adapters — VMs could have their own WWNs and bypass host-level zoning

Check: HPE Alletra VAAI plugin installed from HPE (not third-party substitute)
CLI Command: esxcli software vib list | grep -i hpe
GUI: vCenter: Host > Configure > Software > Installed Packages
Expected (Pass): CLI: VIB list shows HPE-signed VAAI plugin with correct HPE vendor ID and expected version | GUI: Installed Packages shows HPE plugin with HPE as vendor and current version
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: VIB absent or shows non-HPE vendor name for VAAI component | GUI: HPE plugin missing or replaced by third-party package with unverified vendor

Check: ESX lockdown mode enabled on all production hosts
GUI: vCenter: Host > Configure > Security Profile > Lockdown Mode
Expected (Pass): CLI: vim-cmd vimsvc/auth/lockdown_is_enabled returns 'true' | GUI: Security Profile shows Lockdown Mode: Normal (local admin only) or Strict (no local access)
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: returns 'false' | GUI: Security Profile shows Lockdown Mode: Disabled — direct host access bypasses vCenter RBAC and audit trail

Check: ESX Shell disabled on production hosts
GUI: vCenter: Host > Configure > Security Profile > Services — ESX Shell
Expected (Pass): CLI: ESXiShellInteractiveTimeOut = 0 and ESX Shell service stopped (or timeout ≤ 600s if shell is required for break-glass) | GUI: Services list shows ESX Shell: Stopped with Policy: Off
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: ESXiShellInteractiveTimeOut not set or very large; ESX Shell service running | GUI: ESX Shell shows Running or Policy: Start and stop with host — persistent local shell access available

Check: SSH disabled on production hosts
CLI Command: esxcli network firewall ruleset list | grep sshServer
GUI: vCenter: Host > Configure > Security Profile > Services — SSH
Expected (Pass): CLI: sshServer ruleset shows enabled: false | GUI: Services list shows SSH: Stopped with Policy: Off
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: sshServer ruleset shows enabled: true | GUI: SSH shows Running — unnecessary remote shell access exposed on every host

Check: ESX management on dedicated management VLAN (not shared with storage or VM traffic)
GUI: vCenter: Host > Configure > Networking > VMkernel Adapters
Expected (Pass): CLI: esxcli network ip interface list shows vmk0 management adapter on a VLAN/subnet distinct from storage vmk and VM port groups | GUI: VMkernel Adapters shows Management adapter with a different VLAN ID from vMotion / storage / VM traffic adapters
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: vmk0 management IP on same VLAN or subnet as VM or storage traffic | GUI: Management vmkernel shares VLAN ID with other traffic types — management plane reachable from VM network

Check: No shared administrator@vsphere.local — named accounts only in vCenter
CLI Command: Cannot verify via CLI — confirm with team
GUI: vCenter: Administration > Access Control > Roles and Users
Expected (Pass): CLI: N/A | GUI: Users list shows individually named accounts with appropriate roles; administrator@vsphere.local not used for daily operations and its password is controlled
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: N/A | GUI: Only administrator@vsphere.local or generic accounts present; multiple staff using the same credential with no individual audit trail

Check: HBA firmware at current HPE-certified level (check VMware HCL and HPE SPP)
GUI: vCenter: Host > Configure > Storage Adapters — driver / firmware version
Expected (Pass): CLI: esxcli storage san fc list shows driver and firmware version matching HPE SPP and listed on VMware HCL for this ESXi version | GUI: Storage Adapters shows firmware version matching HPE's certified and recommended level
Misconfigured (Fail): CLI: Driver or firmware version not present in current HPE SPP or absent from VMware HCL | GUI: Firmware version mismatches HPE SPP or VMware HCL — may trigger unsupported configuration warnings or expose known vulnerabilities
